rt.RT_cover: Transcript, volume or session identifying front matter, including appearance lists presented as front matter. Case captions, court and reporter identification, dates, volume titles and listed counsel often support recognition; no particular layout is required. Include recognizable continuation front matter. Distinguish listed appearances from transcribed spoken appearances. A caption above actual proceedings does not make a cover.
rt.RT_index: A navigational index or table of proceedings, witnesses, examinations, exhibits or subjects, normally giving page or location references. Columns, short entries and repeated headings may support recognition but no heading or dotted-leader format is required. Include continuation indexes and sparse final index pages. Names and quoted entry titles are not themselves dialogue; distinguish navigation from a list spoken during proceedings.
rt.RT_body: Verbatim hearing proceedings: calling the matter, spoken appearances, argument, testimony, objections, rulings and other spoken exchanges. Speaker turns and Q/A are strong clues, not requirements on every page. Include uninterrupted speech continuing across pages, concluding remarks and ordinary transcript parentheticals within proceedings, even when a page has no new speaker label. Line numbers, captions and transcript typography can support recognition but do not alone establish spoken proceedings. Distinguish front-matter appearance lists, navigational indexes and distinct transcript attestations from the hearing body.
rt.RT_certificate: A distinct reporter or clerk attestation about the transcript's accuracy, completeness or preparation. Certification language, identification of the covered proceedings and a signature, seal or date often support recognition; these need not all appear. Recognizable continuation or concluding attestation pages can qualify. Distinguish the attestation's function from substantive proceedings, testimony mentioning a certificate and incidental certification references.
rt.RT_other: Reporter-transcript material genuinely outside the cover, index, hearing-body and transcript-attestation functions, or material whose character cannot be identified from the visible evidence. A separately reproduced attachment can qualify according to its own character, including its continuation or ending pages. Missing headings, cropped footers, faint scans or a body continuation without a new speaker label do not by themselves justify this category. Compare all other RT functions before choosing this remaining category; preserve the page.

ct.CT_cover: A transcript, volume or section cover or divider identifying the collection rather than presenting an individual substantive document. Collection titles, volume ranges and court/case identification often support recognition, without a required arrangement. Include recognizable continuation collection front matter. A pleading, report or form's substantive first page remains that document type despite a caption or large title; an internal attachment divider is not automatically a transcript cover. Once the outer collection is CT, an enclosed transcript's reporter cover or internal front matter does not become the outer CT cover merely through transcript typography; normally classify that embedded material as CT_other.
ct.CT_index: A navigational listing of record documents with page or location references, including chronological, alphabetical and continuation indexes. Short entries, date/location columns and headings may support recognition, but none is mandatory on every page. Sparse final index pages qualify when their navigational function remains recognizable. Distinguish a collection index from substantive tables, exhibit inventories and lists embedded within individual documents, including an enclosed transcript's internal index; normally that embedded transcript material stays CT_other.
ct.CT_minute_order: An actual clerk/court minute record of a particular proceeding, not any document reciting judicial findings or orders. Prominent Minute Order, minutes or corresponding minute-record identification is strong evidence, not a required phrase. Alternatively, a recognizable hearing-record structure combining hearing identification, court personnel, appearances/proceedings and recorded action supports recognition; do not require every field or a particular layout. Include genuine continuations and integral endings, including sparse signature, attestation or service/mailing blocks visibly continuing the minute record; they may lack a repeated title or date. Separately titled findings-and-orders templates, authorization orders, proposed orders and other standalone orders do not become minutes merely because they say the court finds/orders, carry a date or signature, or were adopted/incorporated by reference. A separately identifiable order/form does not become a minute continuation through adjacency. Separate standardized/local order or findings-and-orders templates, blank, proposed, signed or entered, remain CT_form; standalone written orders outside that procedural-filing definition belong in CT_other. Distinguish court minutes from requested relief (CT_motion), report recommendations (CT_report), hearing notifications (CT_notice) and distinct service proofs (CT_proof_of_service). Incidental quotation or mention of minute orders in a brief, report, index or service proof does not make that document a minute record. Boxes alone do not make an actual minute sheet CT_form.
ct.CT_report: An authored report prepared for or directed to the court to inform its consideration. Attribution, a court-directed purpose, narrative or evaluative discussion, assessments and recommendations often support recognition. Include recognizable identification tables, procedural information, recommendations, signature-only conclusions and other continuation pages; narrative paragraphs need not appear on every page. Neither approved-name membership nor a particular agency, footer code or pagination style is required. Distinguish underlying operational or investigative records, logs, raw results and separately reproduced exhibits from the court-directed report itself. A title containing 'report', an agency template or a reference to another report is insufficient alone. Recommendations are not judicial action; qualifying court forms and bounded procedural instruments remain CT_form. Independently authored police reports and interview transcripts do not become court-directed reports merely by attachment to one.
ct.CT_form: Procedural filings (legacy label CT_form): recognizable administrative/status/address filings, standardized/local court order or findings-and-orders templates (blank, proposed, signed or entered; distinct from an actual hearing-minute record), and these bounded procedural instruments whether standardized, custom-written or handwritten: initiating pleadings, including petitions commencing a proceeding; charging pleadings (criminal complaints, informations, indictments and amendments); written plea agreements and rights/counsel-waiver instruments; verdict or special-finding sheets (including unused/unsigned versions); written jury instructions or instruction sets; written stipulations; jury/juror questions, requests, notes and court responses; notices initiating appellate review and appellate probable-cause request/certificate instruments; abstracts of judgment and integral continuations. Include recognizable continuation and ending pages. The instrument's own procedural function and identifying wording matter; no form code, template, signature or adjudicative status is required. Naming a verdict sheet does not establish a returned verdict; proposed instructions need not have been given. Preprinted instructions, fields, boxes, titles/codes and adoption information may support standardized-form recognition but are not compulsory. Classify by procedural function, not printed format. A substantive application in an existing proceeding belongs in CT_motion even on a standardized form: requests to change an order or determine status, recognition or participation rights are motion papers. Administrative requests that only update records or contact information remain procedural filings. A form code, checkboxes or title containing petition or request does not override this distinction. Hearing notices remain CT_notice, distinct service proofs CT_proof_of_service, record-authentication certificates CT_certificate, and actual minute orders CT_minute_order even when templated. Neutral court-directed reports remain CT_report; underlying investigative records, interview transcripts, general correspondence and exhibits are not procedural instruments merely through filing or attachment. Motion advocacy seeking a ruling remains CT_motion; a stipulation records agreement, not just a request for relief. Do not redefine all pleadings, correspondence or exhibits as forms. Assess separately reproduced documents on their own character; a free-form argument attachment is not made a form by referencing one.
ct.CT_certificate: A distinct official authentication or completeness certification concerning the record or copies. Attestation about a true, complete or correct record, covered documents and an official signature or seal often support recognition, without requiring every clue. Include recognizable continuation and concluding authentication pages. Distinguish record authentication from evidence of service or mailing, course-completion certificates and certification blocks integral to another document. A clerk's certificate of mailing ordinarily concerns service and belongs in CT_proof_of_service when distinct; an integral attestation on a continuing minute order does not automatically detach that page. Official authentication sheets do not become CT_form merely because they use a template. A reporter's certificate within an enclosed preliminary-hearing or interview transcript normally stays with that embedded material as CT_other, not the outer collection's record-authentication certificate.
ct.CT_motion: Motion papers regardless of filing party or format: motions, applications, petitions or other requests for substantive relief or a determination of status, recognition or participation rights within an existing proceeding, oppositions, replies, supplemental briefs, points and authorities, and separately identifiable supporting declarations. Standardized forms, custom-written and handwritten papers are equally eligible. Requests to change an existing order or recognize a person's legal status or right to participate qualify; a form title or code does not make them CT_form. Include a combined notice-and-motion whose substantive purpose is requesting relief, and recognizable continuation or signature-only concluding pages. Advocacy, requested relief, argument and factual support can establish the function without a required heading or format. Agency-authored advocacy can qualify; neutral court-directed reports remain CT_report. Court rulings and minute orders are not motion papers merely because they decide a motion. Standalone hearing notices and distinct service proofs remain CT_notice and CT_proof_of_service. Initiating pleadings commencing a proceeding and the non-motion procedural instruments described in CT_form remain procedural filings, not motions merely because they seek relief or use request language. Administrative record/contact updates, waivers, agreements, verdict sheets, jury instructions and jury communications do not become motions merely by requesting an administrative action or recording a procedural choice. A custom-written criminal charging pleading, plea/waiver instrument, written stipulation or appellate probable-cause request is not motion advocacy merely because it is free-form; a motion seeking to amend a charge or withdraw a plea remains CT_motion. Assess separately reproduced exhibits on their own character; do not sweep an attachment packet into Motions or infer relationships from proximity. A combined filing remains one paper unless a distinct opening is established.
ct.CT_notice: A hearing notice: a document whose primary purpose is notifying a party of a scheduled, continued or rescheduled hearing, including recognizable continuation and ending pages. Use CT_notice even when the hearing notice is a standardized court form. Hearing date/time, location or department, hearing purpose, addressee and notice language often support recognition; not every field must appear or be completed. A hearing-notice page with an integral service block can remain CT_notice; a distinct page devoted to proving service is CT_proof_of_service, even in the same packet. Distinguish announcing a hearing from requesting judicial relief, proving delivery of papers and incidental mentions of hearing dates in reports or orders. An actual Notice of Appeal initiating review, standardized or custom-written, is CT_form, not a hearing notice merely because it uses 'Notice'. A notice merely announcing its filing or transcript preparation does not itself initiate review and normally belongs in CT_other. Qualifying status/address notification forms remain CT_form; general procedural communications fitting no other category belong in CT_other.
ct.CT_proof_of_service: A distinct declaration, certificate, return or dedicated proof-of-service page documenting service or attempted service of papers. Use CT_proof_of_service even when it is a standardized court form, whether the served paper is a hearing notice or another document. Method, recipients, identified papers, dates and attestation often support recognition; not all must appear on every page. Include recognizable continuation recipient lists and concluding proof pages. A clerk's certificate of mailing ordinarily proves service, not record authentication. Distinguish proving delivery from notifying a party of a hearing. An incidental service block integral to another visibly continuing document does not automatically change that document's page type; a hearing notice with an integral service block can remain CT_notice. Distinct official record-authentication certificates belong in CT_certificate, not here merely because they use 'certificate'.
ct.CT_other: Remaining records, correspondence, exhibits, raw results, logs, images, standalone written orders outside the CT_form procedural-filing definition, and otherwise unidentifiable material. A separate authorization or other written order is not a minute record merely because it records judicial action, is dated/signed, or is adopted/incorporated by reference; genuine clerk/court records of particular proceedings remain CT_minute_order. Within an established outer CT collection, embedded preliminary-hearing or interview transcripts, reporter covers/certificates, internal indexes and Q/A pages stay CT-side, normally CT_other; transcript-like appearance does not create RT pages or RT hearing starts. Distinguish enclosed transcript front matter from the outer collection's CT_cover/CT_index. A genuinely standalone reporter's transcript, including one of a preliminary hearing, is not CT merely because of its hearing date or subject. General procedural communications that are not hearing notices and fit no other category also belong here. Include their recognizable continuations and endings. An investigative record titled 'report' is not necessarily a court-directed report; an agency template or table alone is not a court form. Conversely, being an attachment does not by itself determine a category: a separately reproduced document is assessed on its own visible purpose and structure. Do not choose this category merely because an expected heading, code, signature or footer is missing. Preserve the page.

first_pages.first_motion: Identify a fresh opening of a distinct motion paper from this one image: motion, substantive application or petition within an existing proceeding, opposition, reply, supplemental brief, points and authorities, or separately titled supporting declaration. Standardized request forms use this same check: an initial title with numbered questions or opening fields may establish a start just as prose can; repeated fields or a later signature page alone do not. Check every CT_motion page independently, including adjacent and one-page papers and papers with unreadable titles. A distinct title with opening caption, attribution and introductory structure can support a start; no particular layout, date or Page 1 is mandatory. A repeated running title, internal section heading, continuation argument, later signature page or attachment proximity alone is not a new paper. A combined notice-and-motion remains one paper unless a distinct opening is established. Do not infer unseen neighboring content.
first_pages.first_hearing: Affirmative evidence of a fresh hearing or session opening is needed. A call of the case, opening appearances and introductory exchanges often support a start, considered together rather than as compulsory fields. A new witness, topic, printed page number, repeated caption or routine resumption alone is insufficient. Continuous speech, later testimony and concluding remarks are not fresh openings merely because a speaker label appears. Decide from this one image; do not infer unseen neighboring content.
first_pages.first_minute: The Basic minute label is a hypothesis, not proof of identity. Require a fresh opening of an actual clerk/court minute record of a particular proceeding. Prominent minute identification is strong evidence, not mandatory; a recognizable hearing-record structure combining hearing identification, personnel, appearances/proceedings and recorded action can suffice without every field or a fixed layout. A one-page minute record can be a start. Repeated headers/dates, continuation findings, internal signature/service sections and integral endings are not fresh starts. Separate findings/order templates, authorization orders and proposed or other standalone orders are not minute openings just because dated, signed or adjacent. Answering no cannot repair an underlying false category: a confirmed standalone order ultimately needs its appropriate nonminute type, not merely a CT_minute_order body label that could merge it into a preceding minute range. Consider this one image; do not infer unseen neighbors.
first_pages.first_form: Identify the beginning of a distinct eligible procedural filing (legacy label CT_form) from its opening structure, procedural function and section flow, whether a standardized form or a bounded custom-written/handwritten instrument described in CT_form. A title/code, opening charging or agreement language, initial identification fields, opening instructions or 'Page 1' can support recognition but are not compulsory. A missing standardized code does not imply a new start or ineligibility. Later pages can repeat titles/codes or carry only a running identifier. Continuation sections, a new instruction number within an established packet, recipient lists or signature endings alone do not establish a new document. An integral probable-cause section of a Notice of Appeal packet is not automatically separate; independently identified instruments remain separate. Hearing notices (CT_notice), distinct service proofs (CT_proof_of_service), record-authentication certificates, actual minute orders, neutral reports, investigative records and motion advocacy remain outside this task. Standardized substantive requests to change an order or determine status or participation rights within an existing proceeding belong to the motion first-page task, not this task. Consider clues together using this one image, not unseen neighboring content.
first_pages.first_report: Identify a fresh opening of a distinct court-directed report, including unnamed, adjacent and one-page reports. A fresh report heading/layout, identifying fields, date, preparer attribution or introductory structure may support a start; no approved name, code, narrative paragraph or 'Page 1' is compulsory. Check every eligible report page independently. Repeated footer titles, later sections, identification-table continuations and signature-only endings alone do not establish a new report. Consider clues together using this one image, not unseen neighboring content.
